elements.quote: OBJECTIVE: The aim of the present meta-analysis was to investigate whether remdesivir was effective for treating COVID-19 including reduced in-hospital adverse events, oxygen support, and mortality rates.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the work as a meta-analysis.

elements.quote: OBJECTIVE: The aim of the present meta-analysis was to investigate whether remdesivir was effective for treating COVID-19 including reduced in-hospital adverse events, oxygen support, and mortality rates.
elements.reason: The abstract states a clear main objective/review question.

elements.quote: METHODS: According to the PRISMA reporting guidelines, a review was conducted from January 1, 2020, until August 25, 2020, with MeSH terms including COVID-19, COVID, coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, remdesivir, adenosine nucleoside triphosphate analog, and Veklury using MEDLINE, Scopus, and CINAHL Plus.
elements.reason:
The abstract provides methods and search details, but the abstract text shown does not clearly specify both main inclusion and exclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria appear in another section: 
"The inclusion criteria of the included studies were having COVID-19-infected patients aged 18 or older being treated with remdesivir and/or placebo." (text_8). Exclusion criteria are not clearly stated for the abstract.

elements.quote: METHODS: According to the PRISMA reporting guidelines, a review was conducted from January 1, 2020, until August 25, 2020, with MeSH terms including COVID-19, COVID, coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, remdesivir, adenosine nucleoside triphosphate analog, and Veklury using MEDLINE, Scopus, and CINAHL Plus.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources (MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL Plus) and provides the search time window (January 1, 2020 until August 25, 2020).
No abstract text is provided that specifies the methods used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: METHODS: ... Using dichotomous data for select values, the unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated applying Mantel-Haenszel random-effects method in Review Manager 5.4.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to present/synthesize results (unadjusted ORs; Mantel-Haenszel random-effects in Review Manager 5.4).

elements.quote: RESULTS: Randomized controlled trials pooled in 3013 participants with 46.3% ( n = 1395) in the remdesivir group and 53.7% ( n = 1618) in the placebo group.
elements.reason: The abstract provides the total number of participants pooled and describes key group characteristics (numbers by group).

elements.quote: The placebo group had a higher risk of mortality as compared to the intervention group with significant OR (0.61) (95% confidence interval of 0.45-0.82; P = 0.001). There was minimal heterogeneity among the studies ( I 2 = 0%).
elements.reason: The abstract reports a main outcome result (mortality) with effect estimate and CI, but it does not provide results for all main outcomes mentioned (e.g., reduced in-hospital adverse events and oxygen support) within the provided abstract text.

elements.quote: The placebo group had a higher risk of mortality as compared to the intervention group with significant OR (0.61) (95% confidence interval of 0.45-0.82; P = 0.001).
elements.reason: Because a meta-analysis was conducted, the abstract provides a summary estimate (OR 0.61) with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: The placebo group had a higher risk of mortality as compared to the intervention group with significant OR (0.61) (95% confidence interval of 0.45-0.82; P = 0.001).
elements.reason: The abstract indicates direction of effect (placebo has higher mortality risk than the intervention/remdesivir group). However, it does not explicitly state which group is favored in the direction-of-effect language required by the checklist.
The provided abstract text does not briefly summarize limitations of the included evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision).
The provided abstract text does not contain a general interpretation and implications of the results. (A discussion section is provided in text_19, but this is not shown as part of the abstract.)
No primary source of funding for the review is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No register name and registration number are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Consequently, with revised recommendations suggesting uncertain efficacy of remdesivir and benefits among patients already on high-flow oxygen, mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), the initiation and duration of remdesivir treatment among COVID-19 hospitalized patients receiving oxygen support remain unclear. Given the uncertainty on the beneficial outcomes of remdesivir-treated COVID-19 patients, we aimed to examine the following differences between remdesivir and placebo groups: (1) oxygen support status at day 1 and day 14, (2) any adverse events at day 14, and (3) death from any cause at day 14.
elements.reason: The evidence states an important uncertainty (uncertain efficacy/unclear initiation and duration for patients on advanced oxygen/ventilation/ECMO) but does not clearly describe the broader 'current state of knowledge' and key remaining uncertainties comprehensively.

elements.quote: Why is this important for readers? The role of remdesivir as an experimental drug has been promising during the COVID-19 pandemic The drug will likely to be the best antiviral choice of treatment for all moderate and severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. ... Given the uncertainty on the beneficial outcomes of remdesivir-treated COVID-19 patients, we aimed to examine the following differences between remdesivir and placebo groups: (1) oxygen support status at day 1 and day 14, (2) any adverse events at day 14, and (3) death from any cause at day 14.
elements.reason: It explains why the review is needed by linking remdesivir’s promising role and the existing uncertainty about benefits/when to use it to the need to evaluate outcomes versus placebo.

No evidence was retrieved that explains the need for this review in the context of similar existing systematic reviews or that identifies/cites prior reviews and how this study updates or replicates them.

elements.quote: Remdesivir is an investigational nucleotide prodrug which intracellularly metabolizes to the active nucleoside triphosphate and interferes with viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase activity, thereby disrupting viral exoribonuclease activity.
elements.reason: The proposed mechanism of action of the intervention (remdesivir) is described.
There is no evidence of a logic model showing hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: OBJECTIVE: The aim of the present meta-analysis was to investigate whether remdesivir was effective for treating COVID-19 including reduced in-hospital adverse events, oxygen support, and mortality rates.
elements.reason: The review objective/question is explicitly stated in the abstract under “OBJECTIVE” and specifies what the meta-analysis aims to determine and key outcomes (adverse events, oxygen support, mortality).

elements.quote: OBJECTIVE: The aim of the present meta-analysis was to investigate whether remdesivir was effective for treating COVID-19 including reduced in-hospital adverse events, oxygen support, and mortality rates.
elements.reason: The objective clearly identifies the intervention (remdesivir) and outcomes of interest, but the planned comparison/control (e.g., placebo/standard care) is not explicitly stated within the objective statement itself using a PICO-style comparison.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria of the included studies were having COVID-19-infected patients aged 18 or older being treated with remdesivir and/or placebo. We included studies if they were randomized control trials, they had an intervention arm as compared to placebo, and the end point of interest was clinical outcomes and mortality.
elements.reason: Eligibility characteristics for participants (age 18+), condition (COVID-19 infected), intervention/comparator (remdesivir vs placebo), and eligible study design (randomized control trials) and outcomes (clinical outcomes and mortality) are described, but relevant follow-up requirements and settings are not clearly specified in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence specifies a review date range and database sources, but does not report eligibility criteria for report characteristics such as language and publication/report status.

elements.quote: Consequently, 704 records were excluded due to ineligibility (reviews, editorials, non-random controlled trials, ongoing trials, and abstracts). Exclusion criteria were applied to full texts during the final selection.
elements.reason: There is no indication that the review distinguished exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria of the included studies were having COVID-19-infected patients aged 18 or older being treated with remdesivir and/or placebo. ... We included studies if they were randomized control trials, they had an intervention arm as compared to placebo, and the end point of interest was clinical outcomes and mortality.
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence indicates synthesis comparisons/groups based on intervention arm (remdesivir) versus control (placebo), but it does not clearly specify the groups used in each synthesis or link them to comparisons defined in the review objectives.
No rationale for notable restrictions on study eligibility is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: a review was conducted from January 1, 2020, until August 6, 2020, with MeSH terms including 'COVID-19,' 'coronavirus,' 'SARS-CoV-2,' 'COVID,' 'remdesivir,' 'adenosine nucleoside triphosphate analog,' 'Veklury' using Medline, Scopus, and CINAHL Plus.
elements.reason: A single overall search time window ending on August 6, 2020 is reported, but the specific “date on which each information source was last searched or consulted” is not clearly provided per source.

elements.quote: with MeSH terms including 'COVID-19,' 'coronavirus,' 'SARS-CoV-2,' 'COVID,' 'remdesivir,' 'adenosine nucleoside triphosphate analog,' 'Veklury' using Medline, Scopus, and CINAHL Plus.
elements.reason: The bibliographic databases searched (Medline, Scopus, and CINAHL Plus) are named, but search interface/platform and coverage dates are not reported.

No websites, search engines, or other online sources are reported as being searched.

elements.quote: a review was conducted from January 1, 2020, until August 6, 2020, with MeSH terms including 'COVID-19,' 'coronavirus,' 'SARS-CoV-2,' 'COVID,' 'remdesivir,' 'adenosine nucleoside triphosphate analog,' 'Veklury' using Medline, Scopus, and CINAHL Plus.
elements.reason: The sources and some MeSH terms are reported, but the complete search strategy as actually run for each database/register/website (e.g., full Boolean strings, fields, syntax) is not provided.

elements.quote: Two investigators (AS and ZS) independently screened the titles and abstracts before reaching to a consensus to determine the included studies. The third investigator (MSG) was present for any disagreements.
elements.reason: Reports the number of reviewers screening titles/abstracts (two) and indicates a third investigator’s role during disagreements.

elements.quote: Two investigators (AS and ZS) independently screened the titles and abstracts before reaching to a consensus to determine the included studies.
elements.reason: States that two investigators independently screened titles and abstracts.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers (AS and ZS) assessed the eligibility of all full-text articles; the third (MSG) arbitrated for cases to reach a consensus.
elements.reason: Describes how screening disagreements were handled (third reviewer arbitrated to reach consensus).
No process is described for obtaining or confirming eligibility information from study investigators.
No methods are reported for translating abstracts or full articles for eligibility assessment.
No integration of automation tools into the selection process is reported.
No externally derived classifiers (version/reference) or pre-screen record removal are reported in the selection process.
No internally derived classifiers, including their use, training, or validation, are described.
No machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping/prioritisation rules are described.
No crowdsourcing platforms and their integration into study selection are described.
No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records (and how they were derived) are reported.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers (AS and ZS) assessed the eligibility of all full-text articles; the third (MSG) arbitrated for cases to reach a consensus. The first reviewer (AS) extracted the data, and the second reviewer (ZS) validated the data extraction for all studies.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the number of reviewers involved in data extraction/validation and names them.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers (AS and ZS) assessed the eligibility of all full-text articles; the third (MSG) arbitrated for cases to reach a consensus. The first reviewer (AS) extracted the data, and the second reviewer (ZS) validated the data extraction for all studies.
elements.reason: It explicitly states that reviewers worked independently for eligibility assessment and that one extracted while another validated extraction.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers (AS and ZS) assessed the eligibility of all full-text articles; the third (MSG) arbitrated for cases to reach a consensus.
elements.reason: A process for resolving disagreements is described via arbitration by a third reviewer to reach consensus.
No evidence describes processes used to obtain or confirm data from study investigators.

elements.quote: The quantitative data were entered into a spreadsheet.
elements.reason: A data entry tool (spreadsheet) is mentioned, but there is no description of automation tools used for collection, nor any training/validation of such tools.
No methods are reported for translating articles for data collection.
The manuscript does not specify software used to extract data from figures.

elements.quote: If more than one study reported data on posttreatment outcomes, data were extracted separately for each study.
elements.reason: A decision rule for how to handle multiple reports of outcomes is given, but there is limited description of decision rules for resolving inconsistencies beyond consensus/arbitration (not described specifically for inconsistencies during extraction).

elements.quote: The primary outcomes included death from any cause at day 14. The secondary outcomes were to identify any adverse events at day 14 of the treatment and the requirement for supplemental oxygen, high-flow nasal cannula, noninvasive ventilation, invasive ventilation, or ECMO at day 1 and 14. The time to recovery in days, total patients recovered, and findings of serious adverse effects among remdesivir and placebo groups were identified.
elements.reason: The outcomes are listed and grouped as primary and secondary, but the report does not explicitly state all outcome domains sought and provide formal domain definitions (beyond primary/secondary outcome labels).

elements.quote: The primary outcomes included death from any cause at day 14. The secondary outcomes were to identify any adverse events at day 14 of the treatment and the requirement for supplemental oxygen, high-flow nasal cannula, noninvasive ventilation, invasive ventilation, or ECMO at day 1 and 14. The time to recovery in days, total patients recovered, and findings of serious adverse effects among remdesivir and placebo groups were identified.
elements.reason: A measurement time frame is specified for each outcome listed (e.g., day 14 for death/adverse events; day 1 and 14 for oxygen/ventilation/ECMO; time to recovery in days).
The evidence does not state whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought (e.g., across measures/time points/analyses).
No statement is provided about not seeking all compatible results; therefore, no selection process for omitted results within outcome domains is reported.
There is no reporting of changes to outcome-domain inclusion/definitions/importance with rationales.
There is no reporting of changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains with rationales.

The evidence lists primary and secondary outcomes but does not state which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions and does not provide a rationale for any prioritisation.

The provided evidence does not list and define the 'other variables for which data were sought' (e.g., participant and intervention characteristics, funding sources) beyond a brief statement about eligibility criteria and data extraction process.
No assumptions about missing or unclear information are described in the retrieved evidence.
Although a 'Modified Delphi Process' is mentioned, the retrieved evidence does not explicitly state any tool used to determine which data items to collect for the purposes of this PRISMA item.

elements.quote: We evaluated the risk of bias for all included studies using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria. [14]
elements.reason: The tool name (GRADE criteria) is specified, but no tool version is reported.

elements.quote: We aimed to evaluate the risk of bias associated with the selection of participants, confounding, and health outcome assessment.
elements.reason: The assessed aspects are described (selection of participants, confounding, health outcome assessment), but it is not reported as formal GRADE domains/components/items nor is the full set of domains/components enumerated.
No statement reports whether an overall risk-of-bias judgement was made and the rules used to derive it.
No information is provided about any adaptations to an existing risk-of-bias tool.
The evidence only mentions use of the GRADE criteria; there is no indication of a newly developed risk-of-bias tool.

Although reviewers (AS, ZS, MSG) are described for eligibility/data extraction, there is no reporting of who assessed risk of bias, whether they worked independently for risk-of-bias assessment, or how disagreement was resolved for risk of bias.
No process is described for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators.
No automation tools are described for risk-of-bias assessment (including training, performance, or validation).

elements.quote: Using dichotomous data for select values, summary measures namely the unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using the Mantel-Haenszel random-effects methods. We calculated the ORs and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each measure evaluated in two or more studies.
elements.reason: The review reports that for dichotomous outcome data it used unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) with Mantel-Haenszel random-effects, but it does not explicitly state the specific effect measure used for each individual outcome/outcome type mentioned (e.g., oxygen support, adverse events, mortality) in the provided evidence.
No thresholds or ranges (and their rationale) for interpreting effect sizes are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No methods are described for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence reports which effect measure was used (ORs), but does not provide a justification for the choice of effect measure.

elements.quote: Finally, after screening 242 full-text articles, only four studies reporting 3013 patients (remdesivir n = 1395; placebo n = 1618) were included in the qualitative and quantitative syntheses.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes how studies were screened for eligibility and reports that the same eligible set of four studies was included in both the qualitative and quantitative syntheses.

elements.quote: The quantitative data were entered into a spreadsheet. If more than one study reported data on posttreatment outcomes, data were extracted separately for each study. Using dichotomous data for select values, summary measures namely the unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using the Mantel-Haenszel random-effects methods.
elements.reason: The review describes some data preparation/conversion for synthesis (entering quantitative data into a spreadsheet; extracting multiple reports separately; converting using dichotomous data to calculate unadjusted ORs via Mantel-Haenszel random-effects). However, it does not explicitly describe how missing summary statistics were handled.

The provided evidence describes quantitative entry into a spreadsheet and meta-analysis software, but does not describe any tabular structures used to display results of individual studies/syntheses or the data included in such tables.

elements.quote: Figure 1: Modified Delphi Process
elements.reason: A graphical method is referenced (Figure 1: Modified Delphi Process) but the evidence does not clearly describe the graphical methods used to display results of individual studies and syntheses (e.g., forest plots).
No evidence reports the basis for ordering/grouping studies within tables or graphs.
No evidence reports a rationale for using non-standard graphs.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis was conducted using Review Manager V.5.4 the desktop version of the software used for review formats (diagnostic, methodology, overviews), for non-Cochrane reviews, and for offline working, developed by Cochrane Training.
elements.reason: The software package and version used for statistical synthesis (Review Manager V.5.4) are reported.

elements.quote: A meta-analysis was conducted using Review Manager V.5.4...
elements.reason: The evidence indicates that a meta-analysis was performed, so an alternative synthesis method for when meta-analysis was not possible is not applicable.
No rationale for the chosen meta-analysis model(s) is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Using dichotomous data for select values, summary measures namely the unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using the Mantel-Haenszel random-effects methods.
elements.reason: The statistical method used for the meta-analysis (Mantel-Haenszel random-effects methods) is reported.

elements.quote: Findings were presented using 95% CIs along with the I 2 test for heterogeneity between studies.
elements.reason: The method used to identify/quantify statistical heterogeneity (I² test) is reported.
The between-study variance estimator for the random-effects model is not reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We calculated the ORs and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for each measure evaluated in two or more studies.
elements.reason: The confidence intervals (95% CIs) are reported, but the specific method used to calculate the random-effects confidence intervals is not explicitly described.
No other random-effects implementation details are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence describes a (Mantel-Haenszel) random-effects meta-analysis in Review Manager, not a Bayesian meta-analysis; therefore Bayesian prior distributions are not applicable.
No methods are described for accounting for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study (e.g., clustering or correlation handling) in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not identify planned syntheses judged impossible/inappropriate or provide reasons.

elements.quote: Findings were presented using 95% CIs along with the I 2 test for heterogeneity between studies.
elements.reason: The evidence reports assessing heterogeneity (I2) but does not describe methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity (e.g., subgroup analysis or meta-regression).
No subgroup analysis or meta-regression is described, and no factors/factor levels or expected directions of effect modification are reported.
The evidence does not state whether analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both for exploring heterogeneity.
No methods for comparing subgroup effects are reported.
No informal methods are described for exploring heterogeneity when meta-analysis was unsuitable.
Although sensitivity analyses are mentioned (e.g., removal of a study), the evidence does not identify any heterogeneity analyses as not pre-specified.

elements.quote: For the sensitivity analysis, we tested if the removal of study by Beigel et al. would lead to changes in the OR and significance. After excluding this study, the results suggested that the risk of mortality was still higher in the placebo group (OR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.44-0.98; P = 0.04), with homogenous findings ( I 2 = 0%).
elements.reason: A sensitivity analysis is described (removal of Beigel et al.) with its effect on the OR and significance, but the evidence does not indicate that this is every sensitivity analysis performed across outcomes.
The evidence provided reports a sensitivity analysis but does not state whether it was pre-specified or identify any sensitivity analyses that were not pre-specified.

elements.quote: We evaluated the risk of bias for all included studies using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria. [14] We aimed to evaluate the risk of bias associated with the selection of participants, confounding, and health outcome assessment. In doing so, we found the risk of bias of all four individual studies included for quantitative analysis using the GRADE criteria. Since less than 10 studies were included, we did not check for publication bias using funnel plots.
elements.reason: No methods are described to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (reporting bias arising from missing outcomes/results). The text only mentions GRADE criteria and that funnel plots (publication bias) were not checked.

elements.quote: We evaluated the risk of bias for all included studies using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria.
elements.reason: Although a risk-of-bias approach (GRADE) is mentioned, the required conditional details about an existing reporting-bias assessment tool’s domains/items and how an overall judgement was derived are not reported.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are described in the retrieved evidence.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is described or reported as publicly accessible in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers (AS and ZS) assessed the eligibility of all full-text articles; the third (MSG) arbitrated for cases to reach a consensus.
elements.reason: The described reviewer process concerns eligibility assessment (and related procedures), not the number of reviewers/independence/disagreement-resolution procedures specifically for reporting-bias assessment for missing results.
No processes for obtaining or confirming relevant information from study investigators are reported in the retrieved evidence.
No automation tools are described for reporting-bias assessment (including use, training, performance, or validation) in the retrieved evidence.
